new_statements.rule_in_words: Main (primary) stress on the word-initial syllable; nothing known about secondary stress. This is a survey classification without a named descriptive source, explicitly flagged by its author as deduced from scanty archival material and to be handled with caution.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level main stress category in a typological appendix; no data, no examples, no domain discussion. The only published first-hand description of the language (Mathews 1905) says nothing about accent, and Bowern 2001's remark that 'stress at all stages of Karnic is on the initial syllable of the word' (p.253) is generic and made in a paper that doubts Badjiri is Karnic.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the Paroo River language Badjiri/Budjari/Baddyeri (AIATSIS D31 = Glottolog badj1244, ISO jbi; Tindale T227 in Goedemans' numbering). Not to be confused with Maric Bidjara/Bidyara (bidy1243, AIATSIS E37) or the Bulloo River 'Pitjara/Bidjara' dialect of Kalali (kala1380). Mathews' 1905 'Baddyeri' is the same Paroo River group (sections Woongo, Koobaroo, Bunburri, Koorgilla; east of his 'Wonkamurra'). Classification is unsettled: Glottolog files it under Karnic > Badjiri-Eastern Karnic, Bowern 2001 doubts it is Karnic, Breen 2007 calls it 'Karna-Mari fringe', Wikipedia/Dixon lean Maric.

readall_conflicts: No disagreement between sources, because the only primary description (Mathews 1904/05) says nothing about stress. The catalog's initial-stress record therefore rests entirely on Goedemans 1998 Appendix D, which lists 'Badjiri (T227)' under 'II Initial main stress, no info on sec stress' with 'No reference. (Very little information was found.)' and whose intro (p. 235) says such unreferenced entries were deduced from scanty AIATSIS/ANU material and 'must be handled with caution'. the catalog reading stays in place by default, not by new evidence.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2001. Karnic classification revisited. In J. Simpson et al. (eds), Forty years on: Ken Hale and Australian languages, 245-261. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 512.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Badjiri-specific statement. Sec. 5.2.3 'Badjiri' (p.257; data from Mathews 1905 and Breen n.d. Badjiri fieldnotes MS) is purely classificatory and concludes Badjiri probably should not be classed as Karnic. A generic aside on p.253, '(stress at all stages of Karnic is on the initial syllable of the word)', is about Karnic, from which the paper excludes Badjiri.
